Independent review of Crystal Ball PR #1772
Reviewer: Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol (gpt-6.1-sol), medium reasoning.
Reviewed SHA: ce443bbcc351c4f795ed2d86c95931542ad6222a
Reviewed tree: 5f4f427337d5278901f8dc9614c0612b9e54d113
Base SHA: d7e116a576f3038b73fbf2669c66384f6b63feed
Verdict: APPROVE.
Blocking findings: 0.
Other actionable findings: 0.

I reviewed the complete 15-file diff, AGENTS.md, the Crystal Ball feature workflow, and the approved R4-SEC-002 design. The worktree is clean and its HEAD/tree match the frozen candidate. No correctness, security, or regression defect requiring repair was identified in this implementation.

The age gate compares both npm lockfiles and Cargo.lock against the base commit, checks newly introduced registry versions, enforces the seven-day boundary, and blocks unknown publication times unless explicitly approved. Its registry requests use bounded concurrency, timeouts, and the expected npm time[version] and crates.io version.created_at fields. The human gate executes trusted base-branch policy with read-only permissions and no PR checkout; pagination, rename source paths, oversized PRs, and API errors are handled conservatively. The auto-merge skip and best-effort disable behavior match the approved design. The new disable step passes the branch through an environment variable, repairing its template-injection defect. Cooldowns, signature-audit wiring, CODEOWNERS, targeted mappings, tests, and documentation are consistent with the scoped change.

Validation evidence audited, rather than rerun:

- Raw targeted logs report supply-chain: 16 pass / 0 fail; install scripts: 56 pass / 0 fail; agentic pipeline: 65 pass / 0 fail. The combined gate log ends with “Agentic validation gate passed.”
- The current mutation manifest and specifications agree with all 23 nonempty applied diffs and raw assertion failures. Counts are 15 pass / 1 fail for 19 mutations, 14 pass / 2 fail for M02/M11/M13, and 13 pass / 3 fail for M10. Each restoration log reports matching before/after SHA-256 and an empty clean status; I independently compared all restored hashes to the actual frozen final files. Before/after baselines both report 16 pass / 0 fail.
- Current mutation evidence was produced at f8108eba165e6e58d47c7914009b353415966949. The actual diff from that commit to the reviewed SHA contains only the validation document. The older 22-proof run was not treated as current evidence.
- I inspected the live-probe script, JSON, and log: three credential-free requests consumed the production response fields; the unpublished npm sample produced “no publish time.” These attached observations support response-shape compatibility but are a single dated sample, not independent live verification by this offline reviewer.

Limits and remaining validation: local node_modules predates main's dependency fix. Neither a fresh locked install nor npm audit signatures against the current lockfiles has been independently validated here; those remain for the separately approved CI push phase. No local app/desktop install or build was performed. Required status-check configuration remains an external deployment requirement: until configured, the documented checks are advisory. Approval labels are process controls, not human-identity enforcement. Zizmor is not a main CI gate; its new dangerous-triggers finding corresponds to the approved read-only pull_request_target design and does not demonstrate execution of PR code. Existing main findings and downstream #1781/#1785 deltas were not reviewed as this PR's changes.

This is approval of the exact reviewed code SHA, not confirmation of fresh-install CI success or authorization to publish, merge, or install. No code-review blocker remains.
